title: Concrete iterated relative products and finite-module compact-support arrows
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum $P$ and its standard size-lifted finite coefficient ring $A=P.\mathrm{Coefficient}$ [def-pur-conventions]. Use scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], the small pro-etale fixed-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the derived inverse images, tensor products, their unitors and signed symmetries [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define $D_P(T)=D(\operatorname{Sheaf}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{ModuleCat} A))$. For a sequence $X_i\to B$, define the left-iterated product $P_0=X_0$ and $P_{j+1}=P_j\times_BX_{j+1}$ over $B$, with its actual first and last pullback projections. For a single morphism $f:X\to B$, denote its constant-family specialization by $S_j$, with projections $p_j:S_{j+1}\to S_j$ and $q_j:S_{j+1}\to X$. For $M\in D_P(X)$ put $M_0=M$ and $M_{j+1}=Lp_j^*M_j\otimes^LLq_j^*M$. For a compactification $c$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], write $F^c=Rp_*j_!$ for the concrete compact-support candidate [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], and for $c_j$ compactifying $S_j\to B$ put $V_j=F^{c_j}M_j$.

Define the actual finite-module exchange for every pullback square with a specified compactification by inserting the derived proper adjunctions, their inverse-image square comparison, and the inverse canonical open-extension base-change comparison into the proper unit-square-counit/open composite [def-exchange-projection]. Define the compactification projection $\mathrm{PF}_c(K,L):F^cK\otimes^LL\to F^c(K\otimes^LLa^*L)$ by the proper projection morphism, inverse open projection comparison, and pullback-composition identification of the same definition. In the square $S_{j+1}=S_j\times_BX$, specialize exchange to $E_j:Lf^*V_j\to F^{c_j\times_BX}(Lp_j^*M_j)$.

On the full bounded-below etale-origin class [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], define $F_a^{\mathrm{orig}}$ by restricting the selected compact-support candidate. Define its ambient compositor $F_bF_a\cong F_{ba}$ as the unique transport, through the canonical etale-origin equivalence [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], of the ordinary etale compact-support compositor [def-sf-etale-support-compositor], conjugated by the canonical compact-support site comparisons. For quasi-compact $a:T\to U$, $b:U\to W$, $t=ba$, specified compactifications $c_a,c_b,c_t$, and etale-origin $K$, define $C^{-1}_{a,b,K}:F^{c_t}K\cong F^{c_b}F^{c_a}K$ by first comparing $c_t$ with the selected compactification of $ba$, applying the inverse ambient compositor, then comparing the selected compactifications of $b$ and $a$ with $c_b$ and $c_a$, respectively. All these comparisons are the canonical comparisons [def-pur-origin-compactification-comparison].

For $f$ quasi-compact define a stage-domain predicate at $j$ to consist of quasi-compactness of $S_j\to B$, finite-Tor constructibility [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] of $Lp_j^*M_j$, $M$ and $V_j$ on their respective schemes, etale-origin membership of $M_{j+1}$, and invertibility of $\mathrm{PF}_{c_j\times_BX}(Lp_j^*M_j,M)$, $\mathrm{PF}_{c_0}(M,V_j)$ and $E_j$. Given that predicate, define $s_j:V_{j+1}\to V_j\otimes^LV_0$ by the ordered six-factor composite $C^{-1}$, $F^{c_0}(\mathrm{PF}_{c_j\times_BX}^{-1})$, $F^{c_0}(E_j^{-1}\otimes1_M)$, $F^{c_0}(\sigma_{Lf^*V_j,M})$, $\mathrm{PF}_{c_0}(M,V_j)^{-1}$, and $\sigma_{V_0,V_j}$. Set $T_0(V)=V$, $T_{j+1}(V)=T_j(V)\otimes V$; define $\kappa_0=1$ and $\kappa_{j+1}=s_j;(\kappa_j\otimes1)$. For $u:V_0\cong\mathbf1$, define $U_0=u$ and $U_{j+1}=(U_j\otimes u);\lambda_{\mathbf1}$. These are definitions of concrete objects, predicates and arrows; they assert no stage-domain existence or isomorphy conclusion.
